column1: # The red run: this tree's assertions against the engine the base ref holds,
# written whole by tests/red, which tests/run --record-assertions calls.
#   base  <ref>  <sha>  <engine version there>
#   run   <failed>  <passed>  <skipped>        lines counted, not the summary
#   <assertion name>  <times it failed>        failed names only
#   an assertion the manifest lists that the base run never reached counts as failed, by its shortfall
# A base of - means no complete red run was made: none was possible, the
# suite stopped before reached or reached no assertion, or tests/red itself
# was stopped; its stdout said which unless it was the one stopped.
# Reproduce with: tests/red <ref>
base
run
D1: a FELIX_TEST_JOBS the caller already had is replaced by the N this machine gives, from whichever step answers (sysctl or getconf)
D1: only the value true stops it: GITHUB_ACTIONS=false still sets the N this machine gives, from whichever step answers (sysctl or getconf)

D1: with GITHUB_ACTIONS unset gate.sh sets FELIX_TEST_JOBS, for its call to tests/run, to the N this machine gives, from whichever step answers (sysctl or getconf), and its argument list stays --reuse

D1: with GITHUB_ACTIONS unset, gate.sh sets FELIX_TEST_JOBS to the N this machine gives, from whichever step answers (sysctl or getconf: hw.perflevel0.logicalcpu when it answers digits only and at least 1; else hw.ncpu, then getconf, then 1; held to 1 to 64), for its call to tests/run; the order of the steps is pinned by 1294
R51: a performance-core count of 0 falls to hw.ncpu (12), where a count of 6 beside it is used
R51: a performance-core count of 00 falls to hw.ncpu (12), where a count of 6 beside it is used
R51: a performance-core count of 200 is held to 64, so are 65 and the largest N 64 itself, and a count of 6 over the same hw.ncpu is not held
R51: a performance-core count that is empty falls to hw.ncpu (12), where a count of 6 beside it is used
R51: a performance-core count that is not a number (abc) falls to hw.ncpu (12), where a count of 6 beside it is used
R51: a performance-core count that is not digits only (6x) falls to hw.ncpu (12), where a count of 6 beside it is used
R51: a performance-core count whose call fails falls to hw.ncpu (12), where a count of 6 beside it is used
R51: the performance-core count answers first: hw.perflevel0.logicalcpu 6 over a different hw.ncpu 12 gives 6, 8 over 4 gives 8, and a failing hw.ncpu or a getconf does not change it

R51: with the performance-core key (hw.perflevel0.logicalcpu) failing, or set to 0 in one case, hw.ncpu answers, then getconf, then 1, a count above 64 is held to 64, and a non-number falls on, as before; an hw.ncpu of 0 is a number that does not fall to getconf and is held to 1 (R52); a performance-core count of 6 over the same keys is used
R52: a performance-core count of 08 over an hw.ncpu of 12 gives 8 and 09 gives 9 (the leading zero is stripped), and a count of 1 over 12 gives 1
